claims.text: All namespaces of a cluster share one control plane (API server, etcd), one Kubernetes version, the CNI/network plugin, and cluster-scoped objects such as CustomResourceDefinitions and ValidatingWebhookConfiguration/MutatingWebhookConfiguration.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Cluster Architecture; Namespaces > Not all objects are in a namespace; Dynamic Admission Control (webhook configurations are cluster-scoped); Network Plugins

claims.text: Upgrading the control plane changes the API server version for the whole cluster, i.e. for every namespace; a CRD is one cluster-scoped definition, so changing it for one namespace's trial applies to every namespace's objects of that kind.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Upgrading kubeadm clusters; Extend the Kubernetes API with CustomResourceDefinitions (CRDs are cluster-scoped)

claims.text: Each admission webhook configuration has a failurePolicy; when the webhook cannot be called and it is Fail, the API server rejects the requests the webhook covers, in every namespace its rules and namespaceSelector match.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Dynamic Admission Control > Failure policy; Matching requests: namespaceSelector

claims.text: The Kubernetes project documents the cluster sizes it is designed to accommodate (limits on nodes, Pods per node, total Pods and containers); the lesson names nodes and Pods but states no number.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Setup > Best practices > Considerations for large clusters

claims.text: Opinion: add a cluster only for a boundary one cluster cannot hold: trials of upgrades/CRDs/webhooks, a second site that keeps serving, rules forbidding a shared control plane (dedicated nodes still share the API server), documented size limits; else namespaces.
claims.source_hint: trade-off reasoning; Kubernetes docs: Multi-tenancy (isolation, control plane isolation); claims 1-4

claims.text: Opinion: when teams belong to one company and trust each other, namespaces with bindings, policies and quotas usually cost less than a cluster per team, each of which adds a control plane and platform to upgrade; revisit if CRD versions conflict.

Opinion: a second cluster raises availability only if it does not share the first's failure (other site, own control plane, traffic able to move, needed data present); clusters deployed from the same commit can fail together.
claims.source_hint: trade-off reasoning; failover lessons later in this module

claims.text: Opinion: sharing one sealing key across clusters means sealing once, at the price that one leaked private key opens every cluster's secrets; a key per cluster means sealing once per cluster.

Nodes can be dedicated to one tenant's Pods inside a single cluster (node isolation), but those tenants still share the cluster's API server; only a separate cluster (or a virtual control plane) avoids sharing the control plane.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Multi-tenancy > Isolation > Node isolation; Control plane isolation
